result.rationale: The diff shows `<%- end if %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb, which is not valid ERB/Ruby — a bare `if` after `end` cannot legally form a statement. Whether it raises a SyntaxError when the template compiles or (as the finding argues) ambiguously binds the following emitted expression as a modifier condition, it is a real defect introduced by this diff in newly added view code, and no spec renders this view to catch it. The exact parse behavior is hard to verify statically, but the construct is verifiably malformed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the block is closed with `<%- end if %>` (no condition). In Ruby, a trailing `if` is a statement modifier that expects a condition expression; with none provided on the same line, the parser will bind the next emitted Ruby expression (the following `<%= link_to(image_tag(...)) %>` output statement) as the modifier condition. That makes the preceding `if/else` header links render only because the next expression currently evaluates truthy, and any change to that next line can silently change whether the header renders. This is a real template correctness bug, and the provided controller specs don’t render views, so it wouldn’t be caught.
